denseAsDefault.source: results/primer-ablation.json cells['confirm(e+f)/haiku'|'sonnet'|'pooled'], sets e and f (24 tasks per model), fresh Haiku and Sonnet subjects, dense.D0 against the best canonical primer canon.KR3
denseAsDefault.reading: dense wins the 10-task and unbounded session cost on both models and loses the cold single-task cost on both; one-shot acceptance 44 of 48 against 41 of 48 and accepted after repair 45 against 46 of 48 (within noise). So dense as the default would close the session-length token losses and keep the single-call loss; no new run was made for this entry. Superseded by setH: the pre-registered confirmation on set H did not hold, so the 325 dense-view token entries stay open and no shipped-default change is justified by current data.

setH.reading: a new sealed set (H, 16 tasks, pre-registered) did not confirm it: dense one shot 12 and 14 of 16 against 13 and 16 for the best canonical primer, and a higher cost per accepted edit at the 10-task horizon on both models (187.0 against 162.9 Haiku, 120.5 against 114.9 Sonnet); the rule was not met and dense is not recommended.

setI.reading: a second pre-registered confirmation (set I, 16 tasks, 8 with a non-u32 result, after the unwritten-result parser fix) split by model: the rule is met for Sonnet (one shot 16 against 14; 119.9 against 138.9 at 10 tasks) and not for Haiku (12 against 15; 169.7 against 130.5), so it is not met overall and dense is still not recommended. Dense is a candidate for larger models, a loss for the smaller one.
